appName.description: The extension's name. The same in every language.

appDesc.message: View, edit, delete and block cookies. There are no ads, and nothing you do leaves your computer.
appDesc.description: The summary under the name in the Chrome Web Store and on chrome://extensions. 132 characters at most.

cookie_expirySession.description: Short: the Expires column of the cookie table, for a cookie with no expiry date (deleted when the browser closes). One word if possible.

cookie_expiryUnknown.description: Short: the Expires column of the cookie table, when the expiry date can't be read. One word if possible.

cookie_expirySessionFull.message: Session cookie - removed when the browser closes
cookie_expirySessionFull.description: Tooltip on the Expires cell of a cookie with no expiry date.

cookie_expiryUnreadable.message: Expiry date could not be read
cookie_expiryUnreadable.description: Tooltip on the Expires cell when the cookie's expiry date can't be read.

cookie_expiresOn.description: Tooltip on the Expires cell of the cookie table. $1 is the date and time, formatted by the browser, possibly followed by how soon, e.g. "05/11/2026, 14:30:00" or "05/11/2026, 14:30:00 (in 3 days)".

cookie_expiryDateAndRelative.description: A cookie's expiry date with how soon that is. $1 is the date and time, e.g. "05/11/2026, 14:30:00"; $2 is the browser's own wording for how soon, e.g. "in 3 days". Change only the brackets, if your language writes this differently.

cookie_sameSiteUnset.description: Short: a cookie's SameSite setting when none was given. SameSite is a cookie attribute name; this word says it has no value. One word.

cookie_valueAsDateText.description: In the cookie editor, a cookie value that looks like a timestamp, shown as a date. $1 is the date and time in the browser's format, e.g. "Thu, 5 Nov 2026, 14:30:00". "Your time" means the user's own time zone.

cookie_valueAsDate.description: Short: label above the cookie editor's readable view of a value that is a timestamp, shown as a date.

cookie_valueFromBase64.description: Short: label above the cookie editor's readable view of a value that was Base64 and has been decoded. Base64 is a technical name; keep it.

cookie_valueDecoded.description: Short: label above the cookie editor's readable view of a value that was URL-encoded (%7B%22) and has been decoded.

cookie_valueLaidOut.description: Short: label above the cookie editor's readable view of a value that is JSON, shown spread over several indented lines.

cookie_valueNotJson.description: Error in the cookie editor when "Edit as JSON" is ticked and the value doesn't parse. $1 is the browser's own error message, in English, e.g. "Unexpected token } in JSON at position 12".

cookie_bytes_one.description: A size in bytes, in the cookie table and its tooltips. $1 is the number, e.g. "1".

cookie_bytes_other.description: A size in bytes, in the cookie table and its tooltips. $1 is the number, e.g. "812". Short: also used in a narrow table column.

cookie_kilobytes.description: A size in kilobytes, in the cookie table and its tooltips. $1 is the number, e.g. "3.1". KB is the unit; use your language's usual abbreviation.

cookie_knownByOthers_one.description: Who a cookie name is known to be used by, when the database lists it under more than one company. $1 is the number of other companies, e.g. "1"; $2 is the first company's name, e.g. "Didomi". Shown in a tooltip in the cookie table.

cookie_knownByOthers_other.description: Who a cookie name is known to be used by, when the database lists it under more than one company. $1 is the number of other companies, e.g. "3"; $2 is the first company's name, e.g. "Didomi". Shown in a tooltip in the cookie table.

cookie_kindFunctional.description: What a known cookie is for, as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Google, functional." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_kindAnalytics.description: What a known cookie is for, as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Google Analytics, analytics." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_kindMarketing.description: What a known cookie is for, as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Meta, marketing." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_kindSecurity.description: What a known cookie is for, as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Cloudflare, security." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_kindNecessary.description: What a known cookie is for (needed for the site to work), as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Shopify, necessary." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_kindPersonalisation.description: What a known cookie is for (remembering a user's choices to tailor the site), as a word inside the sentence "Known name: Hotjar, personalisation." (see cookie_knownNameKind). Lower case in English because it's mid-sentence.

cookie_knownNameKind.description: In the cookie editor, under the name field, when the cookie's name is in a public database of known cookies. $1 is the company it's listed under, e.g. "Google Analytics"; $2 is what it's for, one of the cookie_kind... words, e.g. "analytics". An English description from the database may follow.

cookie_knownName.description: In the cookie editor, under the name field, when the cookie's name is in a public database of known cookies and the database doesn't say what it's for. $1 is the company it's listed under, e.g. "Google Analytics".

cookie_knownAlsoListed.description: In the cookie editor, after "Known name: ...", when the database lists the name under more companies. $1 is a list of company names, e.g. "Didomi" or "Didomi, Sourcepoint and OneTrust".

cookie_listAnd.description: Joins the last name onto a list of names. $1 is one name or several separated by commas, e.g. "Google, Meta"; $2 is the last name, e.g. "TikTok". Gives "Google, Meta and TikTok".

cookie_errorNoName.description: Error in the cookie editor (or when importing) when the name is empty.

cookie_errorNameCharacters.message: A cookie name can't contain spaces, semicolons, commas or equals signs.
cookie_errorNameCharacters.description: Error in the cookie editor (or when importing) when the name has a character cookies don't allow.

cookie_errorValueSemicolon.message: A cookie value can't contain a semicolon.
cookie_errorValueSemicolon.description: Error in the cookie editor (or when importing) when the value has a semicolon.

cookie_errorTooBig.message: Chrome won't store a cookie bigger than $1 bytes (name and value together). This one is $2.
cookie_errorTooBig.description: Error in the cookie editor when the cookie is too big. $1 is the limit, e.g. "4,096"; $2 is this cookie's size in bytes, e.g. "5,210".

cookie_errorTooBigImported.message: Chrome won't store a cookie bigger than $1 bytes (name and value together). It is $2.
cookie_errorTooBigImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported, when it's too big. $1 is the limit, e.g. "4,096"; $2 is the cookie's size in bytes, e.g. "5,210".

cookie_errorSecurePrefixImported.message: Its name starts with __Secure- but it isn't Secure, and Chrome won't accept that.
cookie_errorSecurePrefixImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported. __Secure- is a name prefix and Secure a cookie attribute; keep both exactly.

cookie_errorSecurePrefix.message: A name starting with __Secure- only works on a Secure cookie. Tick Secure, or change the name.
cookie_errorSecurePrefix.description: Error in the cookie editor. __Secure- is a name prefix and Secure a cookie attribute (and the label of a tick box); keep both exactly.

cookie_hostPrefixSecure.description: One of the things a cookie whose name starts with __Host- must be, listed in cookie_errorHostPrefix's $1. Secure is a cookie attribute; normally kept as it is.

cookie_hostPrefixHostOnly.description: One of the things a cookie whose name starts with __Host- must be (sent to this exact host, not its subdomains), listed in cookie_errorHostPrefix's $1.

cookie_hostPrefixRootPath.description: One of the things a cookie whose name starts with __Host- must be, listed in cookie_errorHostPrefix's $1. "/" is the cookie path; keep it.

cookie_listOr.description: Joins two things a cookie isn't, in cookie_errorHostPrefix's $1. Each is one of cookie_hostPrefixSecure, cookie_hostPrefixHostOnly or cookie_hostPrefixRootPath, or an earlier join, e.g. "Secure or host-only".

cookie_errorHostPrefixImported.message: Its name starts with __Host-, so Chrome only accepts it if it is Secure, host-only and on the path /. It isn't $1.
cookie_errorHostPrefixImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported. $1 is what it isn't, e.g. "Secure" or "host-only or on the path /". __Host- is a name prefix; keep it.

cookie_errorHostPrefix.message: A name starting with __Host- only works on a cookie that is Secure, host-only and on the path /. This one isn't $1.
cookie_errorHostPrefix.description: Error in the cookie editor. $1 is what this cookie isn't, e.g. "Secure" or "host-only or on the path /". __Host- is a name prefix; keep it.

cookie_errorNoDomain.description: Error in the cookie editor (or when importing) when the domain is empty.

cookie_errorPathSlash.message: The path has to start with a slash.
cookie_errorPathSlash.description: Error in the cookie editor (or when importing) when the cookie's path doesn't start with "/".

cookie_errorSameSiteNoneImported.message: It has SameSite “None” but isn't Secure, and Chrome won't accept that.
cookie_errorSameSiteNoneImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported. SameSite, None and Secure are cookie attribute names and values; keep them.

cookie_errorSameSiteNone.message: SameSite “None” only works on a Secure cookie. Tick Secure, or choose a different SameSite.
cookie_errorSameSiteNone.description: Error in the cookie editor. SameSite, None and Secure are cookie attribute names and values (and labels in the form); keep them.

cookie_errorPartitionedImported.message: It's partitioned but isn't Secure, and Chrome won't accept that.
cookie_errorPartitionedImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported. Partitioned (CHIPS) cookies are kept separately for each site. Secure is a cookie attribute; keep it.

cookie_errorPartitioned.message: A partitioned cookie only works when it's Secure. Tick Secure.
cookie_errorPartitioned.description: Error in the cookie editor. Partitioned (CHIPS) cookies are kept separately for each site. Secure is a cookie attribute and a tick box label; keep it.

cookie_errorNoExpiryImported.message: It has no expiry date and isn't marked as a session cookie.
cookie_errorNoExpiryImported.description: Error shown for a cookie in a file being imported.

cookie_errorNoExpiry.message: Set an expiry date, or tick “Session cookie”.
cookie_errorNoExpiry.description: Error in the cookie editor. “Session cookie” is the label of a tick box in the same form; use the same words as that label.

cookie_errorOriginalNotRemoved.message: The original cookie couldn't be removed, so the change was stopped rather than risk leaving two copies of it behind.
cookie_errorOriginalNotRemoved.description: Error in the cookie editor when saving a cookie whose name, domain or path was changed, which means deleting the old one first, and that failed.

cookie_errorNotAccepted.message: Chrome didn't accept the cookie, and didn't say why.
cookie_errorNotAccepted.description: Error in the cookie editor when Chrome refused to save a cookie without giving a reason.

cookie_errorParseOrSet.message: $1 This usually means the domain doesn't match the cookie, or the name or value contains a character cookies aren't allowed to carry.
cookie_errorParseOrSet.description: Error in the cookie editor when Chrome refused a cookie. $1 is Chrome's own error, in English, ending with a full stop, e.g. "Failed to parse or set cookie named \"a\".". The rest explains the usual reasons.

cookie_editTitleEdit.description: Short: heading of the cookie editor screen when editing an existing cookie.

cookie_editTitleNew.description: Short: heading of the cookie editor screen when creating a cookie.

cookie_editPartitionEmbedded.message: Set by $1 in a frame on this site, and kept for this site only (a partitioned, or CHIPS, cookie). Its partition is kept as it is when you save.
cookie_editPartitionEmbedded.description: Note in the cookie editor for a cookie another site set from inside a frame on this one. $1 is that site's domain, e.g. "widget.example". CHIPS is a technical name; keep it.

cookie_editPartitioned.message: This is a partitioned (CHIPS) cookie. Its partition is kept as it is when you save.
cookie_editPartitioned.description: Note in the cookie editor for a partitioned cookie (one kept separately for each site). CHIPS is a technical name; keep it.

cookie_editValueSize.description: Note under the value in the cookie editor, once the cookie is close to Chrome's size limit. $1 is its size, e.g. "3,612"; $2 is the limit, e.g. "4,096".

cookie_editExpiryShortened.message: Chrome shortened the expiry to $1 It limits how far ahead a cookie is allowed to expire.
cookie_editExpiryShortened.description: Added after "Saved changes to ..." or "Created ..." when Chrome moved the expiry date closer. $1 is the date and time it now expires, e.g. "05/11/2027, 14:30:00". The English has no full stop after $1; you may add one.

cookie_editJsonFixIt.message: $1 Fix it, or untick "Edit as JSON" to save it as typed.
cookie_editJsonFixIt.description: Error in the cookie editor when saving a value that doesn't parse as JSON. $1 is cookie_valueNotJson, e.g. "The value isn't valid JSON: Unexpected end of JSON input.". "Edit as JSON" is the label of a tick box in the same form; use the same words as that label.

cookie_editSaved.description: Status line on the main screen after saving an edited cookie. $1 is the cookie's name, e.g. "session_id".

cookie_editCreated.description: Status line on the main screen after creating a cookie. $1 is the cookie's name, e.g. "session_id".

cookie_rowNameTitle.description: Tooltip on a cookie's name in the table. $1 is the name, e.g. "_ga"; $2 is its size, e.g. "40 bytes". Change only the brackets, if your language writes this differently.

cookie_rowEmbeddedNote.message: set in a frame, kept for this site only
cookie_rowEmbeddedNote.description: Small note under the domain in the cookie table, for a cookie another site set from inside a frame on this one (a partitioned cookie). Lower case in English. Keep it short.

cookie_rowEmbeddedNoteTitle.message: Set by $1 in a frame on this site. It's partitioned, so it's kept for this site only.
cookie_rowEmbeddedNoteTitle.description: Tooltip on cookie_rowEmbeddedNote. $1 is the other site's domain, e.g. "widget.example".

cookie_rowPickLabel.description: Screen reader label of the tick box at the start of each table row, used to choose cookies. $1 is the cookie's name, e.g. "_ga".

cookie_rowCopyName.description: Short: a small icon button on a table row that copies the cookie's name. Read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip.

cookie_rowCopyNameTitle.description: Tooltip on the Copy name button. $1 is the cookie's name, e.g. "_ga".

cookie_rowKept.description: Short: label of a row's Keep button when the cookie is already kept (cookieZ won't delete it). One word, read out by screen readers.

cookie_rowKeep.description: Short: label of a row's Keep button: mark the cookie so cookieZ never deletes it. One word, read out by screen readers.

cookie_rowKeptTitle.message: Kept: left out of every delete. Click to stop keeping it.
cookie_rowKeptTitle.description: Tooltip on a row's Keep button when the cookie is kept. Uses the word from cookie_rowKept.

cookie_rowKeepTitle.message: Keep: leave this cookie out of every delete made here
cookie_rowKeepTitle.description: Tooltip on a row's Keep button when the cookie isn't kept. Uses the word from cookie_rowKeep.

cookie_rowEdit.description: Short: label of a row's Edit icon button, read out by screen readers. One word.

cookie_rowEditTitle.description: Tooltip on a row's Edit button.

cookie_rowDelete.description: Short: label of a row's Delete icon button, read out by screen readers. One word.

cookie_rowDeleteKeptTitle.message: Kept cookies aren't deleted. Click the bookmark to allow it.
cookie_rowDeleteKeptTitle.description: Tooltip on a row's Delete button when it's disabled because the cookie is kept. The bookmark is the Keep button's icon.

cookie_rowDeleteTitle.description: Tooltip on a row's Delete button.

cookie_rowDontDelete.description: Short: label of the cancel (cross) button shown next to "Sure?" after Delete is clicked once. Read out by screen readers.

cookie_rowSure.description: Short: a row's Delete button changes to this after the first click; clicking again deletes the cookie. Very tight space: one or two words.

cookie_rowValueEmpty.description: Short: shown greyed in the Value column of the table when a cookie's value is empty.

cookie_rowValueCopy.description: Short: a small button under a cookie's value once it's shown in full in the table. One word.

cookie_rowValueCollapse.description: Tooltip on a long cookie value in the table when it's shown in full.

cookie_rowValueExpand.message: Click to show the full value
cookie_rowValueExpand.description: Tooltip on a long cookie value in the table when it's cut short.

cookie_badgeSecureTitle.description: Tooltip on the "Secure" badge in the table's Flags column. Secure is a cookie attribute and stays in English.

cookie_badgeHttpOnlyTitle.message: Hidden from the page's own JavaScript
cookie_badgeHttpOnlyTitle.description: Tooltip on the "HttpOnly" badge in the table's Flags column. HttpOnly is a cookie attribute and stays in English.

cookie_badgeSubdomains.description: Short: a badge in the table's narrow Flags column, for a cookie that is also sent to every subdomain. One word.

cookie_badgeSubdomainsTitle.message: Also sent to every subdomain of $1
cookie_badgeSubdomainsTitle.description: Tooltip on the Subdomains badge. $1 is the cookie's domain, e.g. "example.com".

cookie_badgePartitionedEmbeddedTitle.message: Partitioned (CHIPS): set by $1 and kept for this site only
cookie_badgePartitionedEmbeddedTitle.description: Tooltip on the "Partitioned" badge for a cookie another site set from inside a frame on this one. $1 is that site's domain, e.g. "widget.example". Partitioned and CHIPS are technical names; keep them.

cookie_badgePartitionedTitle.message: Partitioned (CHIPS): kept separately for each site it's used on
cookie_badgePartitionedTitle.description: Tooltip on the "Partitioned" badge in the table's Flags column. Partitioned and CHIPS are technical names; keep them.

cookie_badgeKnownTitle.message: Known name, used by $1. A guess from the name only.
cookie_badgeKnownTitle.description: Tooltip on the Known badge. $1 is who uses this cookie name, e.g. "Google Analytics" or "Didomi and 2 others" (cookie_knownByOthers).

cookie_badgeKnown.description: Short: a badge in the table's narrow Flags column, for a cookie whose name is in a public database of known cookies. Not "tracker": it's only a guess from the name. One word.

cookie_badgeKnownHidden.description: Read out by screen readers straight after the Known badge (cookie_badgeKnown), so together they say "Known name, used by Google Analytics". Not shown on screen. $1 is who uses the name, e.g. "Google Analytics".

cookie_badgeLarge.description: Short: a badge in the table's narrow Flags column, for a cookie close to Chrome's 4 KB size limit. One word.

cookie_badgeLargeTitle.message: $1. Chrome won't keep a cookie over 4 KB (name and value together).
cookie_badgeLargeTitle.description: Tooltip on the Large badge. $1 is the cookie's size, e.g. "3.6 KB".

cookie_badgeSameSiteStrictTitle.message: Only sent when you're on this site
cookie_badgeSameSiteStrictTitle.description: Tooltip on the "SameSite Strict" badge in the table's Flags column. The badge itself stays in English.

cookie_badgeSameSiteLaxTitle.message: Sent on this site, and when you follow a link to it
cookie_badgeSameSiteLaxTitle.description: Tooltip on the "SameSite Lax" badge in the table's Flags column. The badge itself stays in English.

cookie_badgeSameSiteNoneTitle.message: Also sent when another site loads something from this one
cookie_badgeSameSiteNoneTitle.description: Tooltip on the "SameSite None" badge in the table's Flags column. The badge itself stays in English.

cookie_reportPurposeMarketing.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for. Keep it short.

cookie_reportPurposeAnalytics.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for (measuring visits). Keep it short.

cookie_reportPurposePersonalisation.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for (remembering choices to tailor the site). Keep it short.

cookie_reportPurposeFunctional.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for (features of the site itself). Keep it short.

cookie_reportPurposeSecurity.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for. Keep it short.

cookie_reportPurposeNecessary.description: Site report: a row heading in the table of what the site's cookies are for. Keep it short.

cookie_reportCompaniesOthers_one.description: Site report: the companies behind one row's cookies, when there are more than fit. $1 is how many more, e.g. "1"; $2 is the first few names, e.g. "Google, Meta, TikTok".

cookie_reportCompaniesOthers_other.description: Site report: the companies behind one row's cookies, when there are more than fit. $1 is how many more, e.g. "2"; $2 is the first few names, e.g. "Google, Meta, TikTok".

cookie_reportNotRecognised.description: Site report: the row for cookies whose names aren't in the database of known cookies. Keep it short.

cookie_reportCheckNotSecure.description: Site report, "worth checking" table: a row heading for cookies without the Secure flag.

cookie_reportCheckNotSecureNote.message: They don't have the Secure flag.
cookie_reportCheckNotSecureNote.description: Site report: the small note under cookie_reportCheckNotSecure. Secure is a cookie attribute; keep it.

cookie_reportCheckReadable.description: Site report, "worth checking" table: a row heading for cookies without the HttpOnly flag.

cookie_reportCheckReadableNote.message: They don't have the HttpOnly flag.
cookie_reportCheckReadableNote.description: Site report: the small note under cookie_reportCheckReadable. HttpOnly is a cookie attribute; keep it.

cookie_reportCheckSameSiteNone.message: Sent when another site loads this one
cookie_reportCheckSameSiteNone.description: Site report, "worth checking" table: a row heading for cookies with SameSite None.

cookie_reportCheckSameSiteNoneNote.description: Site report: the small note under cookie_reportCheckSameSiteNone. SameSite and None are a cookie attribute and its value; keep them.

cookie_reportCheckLarge.description: Site report, "worth checking" table: a row heading for very large cookies.

cookie_reportCheckLargeNote.message: A site with too many of these can stop logins working.
cookie_reportCheckLargeNote.description: Site report: the small note under cookie_reportCheckLarge.

cookie_reportCheckSoon.description: Site report, "worth checking" table: a row heading for cookies that expire within 24 hours.

cookie_reportCheckSoonNote.message: A sign-in held in one of these won't last.
cookie_reportCheckSoonNote.description: Site report: the small note under cookie_reportCheckSoon.

cookie_reportShowThem.description: Short: a button in each row of the site report's "worth checking" table; it goes back to the cookie table filtered to those cookies.

cookie_reportShowThemLabel_one.description: Screen reader label of the Show them button. $1 is the number of cookies, e.g. "1"; $2 is the row heading, e.g. "Expire within a day".

cookie_reportShowThemLabel_other.description: Screen reader label of the Show them button. $1 is the number of cookies, e.g. "4"; $2 is the row heading, e.g. "Expire within a day".
